subject: Discovery recap - inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap - inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Alex -

Thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed set of next steps so we stay aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

TL;DR: main pain = inference unit economics at scale. FinBot needs a path to reduce per-call token cost while preserving latency and accuracy for fraud-detection prompts. You're open to model quantization and caching/batching, but need SLOs and predictable cost savings.

What we heard (pain points)
- Current spend: inference is ~40% of LLM feature cost and growing as volume scales.
- Latency sensitivity: fraud detection paths require <=250ms 95th for short prompts (50-150 tokens).
- Existing infra: in-house endpoints on GCP (NVIDIA A100), limited autoscaling, no KV prefix cache today.
- Operational pain: difficulty predicting monthly spend; spikes during peak business hours.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- Reduce per-token cost by >=30% while keeping 95p latency <300ms for production routes.
- Stable throughput at peak with predictable billing and clear fallback if capacity tightens.
- Roadmap to pilot in <8 weeks and production-ready in Q3.

Technical openness and constraints
- Quantization: Alex said FinBot is open to 8-bit/4-bit quantized models for non-sensitive scoring paths, but will require validation for accuracy regressions.
- Caching/Batching: They expect automatic prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching to be leveraged. Rough target: batching + cache should cover ~20-40% of token volume on typical flows.
- Data controls: must be VPC-restricted for production and SOC2 compliance is a requirement.

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood to share an evaluation checklist + architecture notes (attached). Ben will follow up with a short technical note on batching and cache behavior.
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with FinBot SREs + ML infra (Ben + Rishi + Alex + Priya if needed) - propose Tue/Thu next week.
3) Redwood to produce a back-of-envelope cost model showing current vs projected per-token unit economics with quantization and caching assumptions.

Attachments: redwood-eval-checklist.pdf (evaluation checklist), architecture-diagram.png (high-level routing + cache diagram).

I'll follow up with specific times for the technical deep-dive. Thanks again - excited to see if we can give you a predictable, cost-effective path to scale inference.

Best,

Subject: Re: Discovery recap - inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks Marissa - this is an accurate summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Current monthly inference spend (avg): ~$48k; peak monthly was $72k last quarter during a promo window. We need to get to <$35k/month for the current feature set given other product budgets.
- Accuracy floor: any change (quantization or smaller model variant) must keep fraud-detection precision within 1.5% of current baseline on our evaluation set.
- Batching: our team expects batching to be implemented transparently behind endpoints (we want minimal changes in client code). If batching increases tail latency beyond ~50ms, that will be a non-starter for the high-priority route.

We're open to an 8-bit quantization pilot for background scoring jobs; for the real-time fraud route we want aggressive validation first.

Next steps for us: I'll loop in our ML infra lead, Priya Rao, for the technical deep-dive. Tue morning (PST) works best. Also please send the cost model you mentioned - that will help our finance lead triage the procurement timeline.

Appreciate the practical list and attachments - looking forward to the technical session.

Best,
Alex
Director of Engineering | FinBot
alex.johnson@finbot.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - inference cost pressure & next steps

Alex - quick technical note before our deep-dive:

- Batching behavior: Redwood's serving runtime adapts batch size based on warm-up, model latency characteristics, and SLOs. For your 50-150 token prompts we typically see effective batching of 4-8 requests without affecting 95p latency when running on A100 or equivalent; on smaller GPUs the numbers differ and we'll measure during the pilot.
- KV/prefix caching: can be enabled per-route. For short prompt patterns where users repeat prefixes (common in fraud rules), cache hit rates of 15-35% are realistic and lead to >25% token cost reduction on those routes.
- Quantization: we'll run a 8-bit and a 4-bit pilot on a snapshot of your eval set and report delta on precision/recall. We'll gate rollouts on the 1.5% accuracy floor you mentioned.

I'll attach a short pilot plan to the shared Drive link and bring detailed perf numbers to the session.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
